pairs.subject: trust-base
pairs.evidence: eslint.config.mjs:602 The lint block scoped to e2e/**/*.ts applies only the transaction and route-import selectors, with no type-aware unsafe-flow rule. So the many `(await res.json()) as {…}` sites in the specs reach typed assertions without any check, and no census counts them: a directive count over this context reports zero members.

techniques.evidence: e2e/activity-detail.spec.ts:93 A response body typed as the unchecked type is asserted into a hand-written shape with nothing checked at runtime. The same shape repeats across token-doors-axe, quality-tables, profile-roster, profile-builder, journey-one-thread, app-master-hire and journey-role-to-schedule, and no type-aware lint or ratchet counts these members. The technique's cure, decoding to `unknown` and passing the value through one checking function, is used nowhere. activity-detail.spec.ts:76 declares `lastTask: unknown` but then casts it with `as` instead of checking it.

e2e/profile-builder.spec.ts:36 Each cast is sound only if the route's response matches a shape declared elsewhere. BuildResponse, ProfileGet and ActivityRow are hand-written copies that neither name the route declaration they depend on nor get named back by that route. journey-one-thread.spec.ts's BoardEntry doc comment (lines ~530-535) names its source routes, but that note has only one end.

e2e/fixtures/mock-personas-bridge.ts:2 No prover or trusted-body construct exists. The closest analogue is the hand-written Personas mock that the suite trusts, and it does have an outside drift test: scripts/app-master-bench/personas-contract.test.mjs probes it against a contract derived from the real bridge client. That is the technique's spirit, but its precondition does not hold.

e2e/app-master-hire.spec.ts:150 No proof states a platform fact. The suite's environmental premise, a keyless server, is asserted on every turn with a message naming the missing setting. That is the runtime analogue of the build-side assertion, not a proof/build pair.

pairs.registryProposal: census-counts-unmarked-members names annotated callbacks as a shape the type-aware lint misses. It should also name the plain assertion over the unchecked type, `(await res.json()) as Shape`: the most common member in test suites, where the assertion keyword is present but asserts from an unchecked value. Whether the unsafe-flow lint family reports it depends on enabling the separate type-assertion rule, so the technique should say which rule visits this shape.
